title: Changing magnitude-type weights account for most of a larger-event share drop in a 2020 Puerto Rico catalog sample
abstract: We tested how a change in catalog magnitude types affects an observed change in earthquake size. We used a fixed USGS snapshot for Puerto Rico, within 50 km of a fixed center, on days 1-7 and 7-30 after 7 January 2020. Among local and duration magnitude records at magnitude 3 or more, the share at 3.5 or more fell from 47.50% to 28.12%. A symmetric two-part calculation assigned 15.71 percentage points of this 19.38-point drop to changes in type weights. It assigned 3.67 points to changes within types. Conditional 95% two-day block intervals were -20.91 to -10.15 points for the type-weight term and -11.59 to 2.97 points for the within-type term. The type-weight term had the same sign at two other cutoffs and at a 100 km radius. This is an arithmetic result for selected catalog records. Type choice can depend on event size and detection. Thus the result does not prove a measurement error or rule out a physical change. The study adds a type-weight check to a prior campaign forecast test. Code, raw data, event rows, resample values, and an independent arithmetic check are included.

display.caption: Left: the share of events at magnitude 3.5 or more within each magnitude type. Counts give tail events over all events at magnitude 3 or more. Right: the change in the combined ML and MD sample and its two arithmetic terms. Bars give conditional 95% two-day block intervals. The terms do not identify a cause.

citations.reason: We reuse its shared raw snapshot and time and radius settings. It reported the magnitude-type shift. We add a new arithmetic decomposition and block resamples.
Prior public aftershock forecast study reports changes in the magnitude distribution and fitted parameters. We used its public USGS abstract.
The public abstract describes the complex fault network and a much denser catalog. We do not use that enhanced catalog.
USGS definitions distinguish local and duration magnitudes.
